Subject: Warm prefix economics and budget check

Hi Liam / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the call this morning. Quick recap and a focused follow-up so we can align on economics and next steps. I tried to keep this short and action-oriented.

What we heard on the call (short):
- Primary workload: multi-turn assistant for product recommendations + user history (avg session ~ 275 tokens/user request, 1.6 turns/session).
- Expected scale: pilot target ~ 500k tokens/day, scale target ~ 5M tokens/day within 6–9 months.
- Target budget range: looking to keep infra $/1M tokens in the range of $600–$1,200 (company target is $700 mid-band).
- Key constraint: some prompts are highly templated (system + initial instructions) and repeat across sessions — good opportunity for prefix caching.

Attached: prefix cache modeling workbook (20261203_prefixcache_modeling.xlsx) — a quick scenarios tab with the numbers below.

Quick baseline pricing assumptions (for conversation):
- Redwood list price for chosen model variant (r-medu-1): $60 per 1M tokens (batch/hosted rate for generation + context).
- Optional dedicated quantized variant estimate: $40 per 1M tokens (approx list committed price).
- Cache storage amortized overhead (estimated): $800/month for a warm prefix store for the pilot (includes KV storage + minimal sync ops).

Illustrative effective $/1M tokens (no network or app costs included):
- No prefix cache (0% hit): $60 / 1M tokens effective
- Moderate prefix hit (25%): effective = $60 * (1 - 0.25) + cache amortization
  - Example: 0.75 * $60 = $45; pilot amortization (@500k tokens/day ≈ 15M/mo) = $800/15M ≈ $53 / 1M => total ≈ $98 / 1M
- Strong prefix hit (60%): 0.4 * $60 = $24; amortization (@15M/mo) = $53 => total ≈ $77 / 1M

Notes on the arithmetic above: the amortization per 1M is highly dependent on volume; at scale (5M tokens/day ≈ 150M/mo) that same $800/mo becomes ~ $5.3 / 1M, which materially improves the effective $/1M. The workbook has the scaling tab that runs these scenarios.

Questions for you (fast):
1) For pilot sizing — do you expect 500k tokens/day to be sustained (steady) or is that peak daily?
2) Are there specific prompts (system or initial-user templates) you know will be identical across >80% of sessions? If so, the prefix cache hit could be far higher than our conservative 25% above.
3) Is the $700 / 1M target a hard stop or a guideline? That informs whether we recommend dedicated capacity or hosted with cache.

Proposed next steps:
- We (Karthik + Marissa) will produce 2 pager: 1) pilot economics with prefix-cache scenarios at 15M/mo; 2) scale economics at 150M/mo with dedicated pricing (deliver by EOD tomorrow).
- You share any example prompt templates (redacted) or a 48-hour sample of request shape so we can surface likely cacheable prefixes.
- Quick follow-up call next week to walk the workbook.

If that all sounds fine I'll queue the modeling run and attach the pilot M.A.P. (in Drive) to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,

Liam — great context, thanks. Quick technical/economics note and an updated run based on your details. I also attached a copy of the small modeling sheet into the Drive link Hannah shared.

Assumptions I used for a tightened pilot model (15M tokens/mo):
- Base hosted price (r-medu-1): $60 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated committed estimate (quantized): $40 / 1M tokens (requires 3-month commit)
- Cache amortization: $800 / month for the warm-prefix KV store (single region)
- Pilot cap: $12k / month (your ask)

Scenario table (effective $/1M, pilot volumes = 15M/mo):
- No cache (0%): 60.00 / 1M => Monthly = 15 * 60 = $900
- 25% prefix hit: effective unit = (0.75 * 60) + (800/15) = 45 + 53.33 = $98.33 / 1M => Monthly = 15 * 98.33 ≈ $1,475
- 50% prefix hit: effective unit = (0.5 * 60) + 53.33 = 30 + 53.33 = $83.33 / 1M => Monthly ≈ $1,250
- 70% prefix hit: effective unit = (0.3 * 60) + 53.33 = 18 + 53.33 = $71.33 / 1M => Monthly ≈ $1,070

Observations:
- At pilot volumes the cache amortization dominates the per-1M math until you reach higher hit rates (>70%) or increase volume. Because your pilot budget cap is ~$12k, all of the above are well within the cap — so budget is less of an absolute blocker at pilot. The economics question is more about the trajectory to scale where dedicated pricing unlocks better per-1M economics.
- If we model scale at 150M/mo (5M/day): the amortization becomes $800/150 ≈ $5.33 / 1M, so the same 50% hit scenario on dedicated pricing looks like: dedicated base $40 * 0.5 + 5.33 ≈ $25.33 / 1M. That's a material delta.

Cache strategy recommendation (short answer):
- For your workload, a two-tier prefix approach usually works best:
  1) global warm-prefix store for deterministic system and onboarding prompts (highly cacheable across users) — cheap and high hit for the first-turn tokens;
  2) lightweight per-session KV for user-specific small-state (only when user sessions show repeated behavior).
- Global warm-prefix gives the biggest bang-for-buck during pilot because it captures identical system + onboarding tokens across users. Per-session warm cache is valuable at scale for heavy returning users but increases sync complexity.

Action items I can take this morning:
- Run the workbook with your 6 system prompts to estimate an expected prefix hit rate (conservative & optimistic).
- Produce a short slide with break-even volume for moving from hosted+cache to dedicated.

If you share the redacted templates, I'll drop the updated numbers into the Drive file and ping you.
